cards.text: Jesus is sending out His twelve disciples, and He's been honest with them: if people called the head of the house Beelzebul, they'll call His household worse. Then He says, "So do not be afraid of them." Baker, I used to jump every time that junk drawer rattled, so I need to hear this one TWICE.

cards.question: Jesus gives His disciples a reason not to fear the people against them. What does He say about everything concealed and hidden?

answers.text: It will all be made known
It will stay hidden for good

cards.text: Then Jesus talks about what He tells His disciples in the dark, the lean-in-close, whispered-in-your-ear stuff. The kind of thing you only tell your most trustworthy mixing bowl.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells His disciples to keep what He whispers to them a secret.

cards.text: NOPE, Jesus tells them what He says in the dark, speak in the daylight, and what's whispered in their ear, proclaim from the housetops. The HOUSETOPS, baker, and I still whisper when I confess I ate the cookie dough.
Then Jesus says the people against them can kill the body, but there's something they can't touch. Baker, I'm leaning so far off my gold base right now, and don't worry, the base is leaning with me.

cards.question: They can kill the body, but Jesus says they cannot kill the ___.
So instead of fearing those who kill the body, who does Jesus tell His disciples to fear?

answers.text: The One who can destroy soul and body
The governors who judge them in court
The councils that hand them over

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, "Are not two sparrows sold for a penny?" Two birds. ONE penny. You can't even get a single SPRINKLE for that.

cards.question: Two sparrows, one penny. True or false: Jesus says not one of them falls to the ground apart from the will of the Father.

cards.text: Then Jesus says even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Now look at this mustache, baker. That is NOT a small number.

cards.question: Sparrows cared for and hairs all numbered. What does Jesus tell His disciples they're worth?

answers.text: About the same as two sparrows

cards.text: Then Jesus says everyone who confesses Him before men, He will also confess before His Father in heaven. Baker, the nicest thing anybody ever said about me was a price sticker, and it said 25 cents.

cards.question: Jesus promises to confess before His Father everyone who confesses Him before men. True or false: He says He will still confess before His Father whoever denies Him before men.

cards.text: Then Jesus says don't assume He came to bring peace to the earth. Baker, I just dropped my rolling pin, and it bounced off my gold base TWICE.

cards.question: Jesus says He has not come to bring peace. What does He say He has come to bring?

cards.text: Jesus says He has come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. I had to read that one twice, baker, and I don't even HAVE a mother-in-law.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says a man's enemies will be the members of his own household.

cards.text: Then Jesus says anyone who loves father or mother, or son or daughter, more than Him is not worthy of Him. And this is landing on a stamper who named his ENTIRE bakery after his kids.

cards.question: Jesus says anyone who doesn't take up something and follow Him isn't worthy of Him. What does a follower take up?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Whoever finds his life will lose it." Find it and LOSE it? Baker, that's me and my oven mitts every single morning.

cards.question: And whoever loses his life for Jesus' sake will ___ it.

cards.text: Now Jesus talks about the people the disciples will meet out there, the ones who receive them and welcome them in. Baker, back in that junk drawer I WAS the welcome committee, a committee of one, with a scared can opener crying on my mustache.

cards.question: When someone receives the disciples, who else does Jesus say they receive?

answers.text: Jesus and the One who sent Him

cards.text: Then Jesus talks rewards, starting with someone who receives a prophet because he is a prophet. REWARDS, baker. I perk up at that word like the oven timer just went off.

cards.question: Someone receives a prophet because he is a prophet. True or false: Jesus says that person will receive a prophet's reward.

cards.text: Same goes for receiving a righteous man because he is a righteous man. Then Jesus goes small, crumb-on-the-counter small: even a cup of cold water, given to one of these little ones because he's His disciple.

cards.question: Even for one cup of cold water, Jesus says that giver will never lose his ___.
After Jesus finishes instructing His twelve disciples, what does He do next?

answers.text: Teaches and preaches in their cities
Rests for a while in Capernaum
Goes up a mountain alone to pray

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 7 quotes "Whoever finds his life will lose it.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Every baker sees this story card no matter what they picked on card 4. It opens with "NOPE," which reads as a verdict on the baker's answer. A baker who picked True is told no. Reactions to answers belong in the answer explanations, not on a story card.

rule.text: Never says "wrong," "fail" or "bad" about a baker's answer. The reaction phrases for right and missed answers are in answer-explanations.md.

findings.problem: This sentence is garbled: "Jesus tells them what He says in the dark, speak in the daylight, and what's whispered in their ear, proclaim from the housetops." It reads as though Jesus is reporting what He says rather than giving a command. Split it into short sentences that clearly give the instruction, for example: Jesus tells them to speak in the daylight what He tells them in the dark.

The question opens with "Sparrows cared for." Matthew 10:29 never says the sparrows are cared for. It says not one of them falls to the ground apart from the will of your Father. Use the text's own idea, such as "Not one sparrow falls apart from the Father's will."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke says "the nicest thing anybody ever said about me was a price sticker." That contradicts his backstory, where his kids call him Papa and Papa is the best name he's ever been called. The joke also misses the core action. Jesus confessing someone before His Father is about being acknowledged in front of others. A price sticker is about low worth, which fits the sparrows in verse 31, not confessing in verse 32.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the action of the fact. The verse is about Jesus acknowledging a person before His Father. The comparison is about a cheap price tag.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Story card 3 has just told that Jesus turns a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. The true or false statement that a man's enemies will be his own household then can't really be false. The setup leaves no reasoned path to False, so the card tests nothing new. Ask about the meaning instead, or fold verse 36 into the story card and ask a different question.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This setup says "Jesus talks rewards, starting with someone who receives a prophet because he is a prophet." Card 12 then asks true or false whether that person receives a prophet's reward. The setup already pairs receiving a prophet with a reward, so it rules out False. Remove "rewards" from the setup, or ask a question the setup doesn't answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to his backstory: the can opener was "crying on my mustache." The backstory only says the can opener was scared and confused and sure it had done something wrong. Jokes may invent small moments around his bakery, but they don't add to the drawer story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
